desc: THE single blocker for a multi-core daily driver on t6040. Under SMP, the first userspace process after switch_root SIGSEGVs with copy_page -> copy_user_highpage -> do_wp_page, i.e. copy-on-write page copying corrupts or writes a page it must not. Supersedes the narrow unpack_to_rootfs framing in 121: the SAME fault hits ordinary CoW with a 1.8 MB initramfs and no unpack pressure. EVIDENCE: maxcpus=1 -> zero call traces, clean system, repeatedly; maxcpus=4 -> SIGSEGV (exitcode 0x0000000b) + panic; maxcpus=3 and 5 -> hang; maxcpus=4 booted the 99 MB i3 image once. Non-monotonic => a RACE whose window widens with the amount of page copying. REPRODUCER (fast, reliable, no enrollment): boot initramfs-sdroot.cpio.gz with EXTRA_BOOTARGS='maxcpus=N console=ttydc0 sdroot.shell' -- switch_root execs a bare shell, so the very first userspace CoW either survives or panics within ~4 s. Faulting instruction was a8300c02 (stp, a store). LINES OF ATTACK, cheapest first: (1) find the maxcpus threshold precisely with the reproducer (2 vs 3) since 2 may be usable and is untested; (2) suspect cache/TLB maintenance on this core generation -- Everest/Sawtooth mixed clusters, check whether flush_dcache_page / __sync_icache_dcache / the CoW copy path needs an Apple-specific barrier, and whether the fault only occurs when the two threads land on DIFFERENT cluster types (test by pinning cores from ONE cluster only via a c2probe-style DTB); (3) try CONFIG_ARM64_WORKAROUND_* / idle=nop interaction -- we always boot idle=nop because M4 loses CPU state on WFI, which changes the timing of every idle core; (4) bisect a minimal C reproducer (fork + write to a shared page in a loop) so it can be reported upstream without the boot machinery. Check whether yuka/upstream have seen this on t8132; it may be a known M4 erratum. ROUND 1 RESULT 2026-08-03: THRESHOLD = 2 is the limit. maxcpus=1 fully clean; maxcpus=2 runs but the fault still fires on non-init processes (arm64_force_sig_fault -> make_task_dead) so processes randomly die; maxcpus=3/4 kill PID 1 -> panic; 5 hangs. INTRA-CLUSTER HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: dts/t6040-j614s-dcuart-onepercluster.dts gives one CPU per cluster (verified from MPIDRs in the boot log: CPU1 0x0 midr 0x611f0541 E-cluster0, CPU2 0x10200 midr 0x611f0551 P-cluster2) and it STILL panics with the same copy_page fault -- so it is core COUNT, not cluster placement. NON-TEMPORAL hypothesis also refuted: copy_page.S uses plain ldp/stp, no ldnp/stnp. Fault detail: pc copy_page+0x48, lr copy_highpage+0x70, both x0/x1 kernel linear-map, victim gets SIGSEGV. NEXT: minimal C reproducer runnable at maxcpus=2 (where the system survives) to decouple from the boot machinery and make it upstream-reportable; then idle=yield vs idle=nop at maxcpus=3; then CoW cache-maintenance review; then ask upstream whether t8132 shows this.
